subject: Recap: StreamlinePay discovery — budget constraints & token-econ levers
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@streamlinepay.com>, Jae Park <j.park@streamlinepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: StreamlinePay discovery — budget constraints & token-econ levers

Hi Alejandra / Jae —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side so we’re all aligned and the asks are actionable. I pulled this together while it’s fresh — please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you articulated:
- High per-call cost on existing LLM provider given high avg token length (~1.2k tokens per session) and heavy system+context tokens.
- Service-level variability during peak churn (end-of-month reconciliation spikes).
- Procurement cap: public cloud spend for inference is being capped at ~$120k / quarter for pilot stage.

Business goals for pilot (60–90 days):
- Validate a production path that reduces per-conversation inference cost by >= 25% while keeping 95th pct latency < 600ms for short flows.
- Demonstrate predictable economics for month-end peaks (quantify cost at scale).
- Produce a go/no-go recommendation for a scoped production rollout.

Immediate levers & hypotheses we discussed:
1) Token economics optimization — using batching + sticky KV-caching for repeated session prefixes should reduce token compute by ~20–35% on your traffic profile.
2) Model variant routing — mix a lower-cost quantized model for background flows, fallback to a higher-accuracy variant for critical paths.
3) Dedicated capacity for predictable latency during spikes (trade versus burst pricing).

Next steps (agreed):
- I’ll send a short token-econ model and a pilot one-pager (attached) with a baseline vs. 3 pilot configurations.
- You’ll confirm the internal budget band (approx upper/lower bound within the $120k / quarter cap) and share the procurement contact(s) to loop in.
- Marissa will join next week’s technical kickoff to review latency SLOs and observability hooks.

Attachments: streamlinepay_token_econ_model.xlsx (token-econ workbook), redwood_pilot_onepager.pdf (pilot scope / milestones).

Open questions we flagged:
- What percentage of calls must hit the 95th pct latency SLO versus acceptable tail exceptions? (helps size dedicated pool)
- Any regulatory/retention constraints for logs or embeddings for out-of-scope users?

If you’re good with this wording I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff next Tue or Wed and loop in procurement once we have the budget band.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@streamlinepay.com>

Subject: Re: Recap: StreamlinePay discovery — budget constraints & token-econ levers

Thanks, Karthik — this is great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget guardrails: procurement has set a soft cap at $120k / quarter for vendor pilots. We can stretch to $150k for a pilot that clearly demonstrates >= 30% savings in per-conversation cost with comparable latency.

2) Latency targets: for customer-facing flows we need 95th < 600ms and 99th < 1.2s ideally. Internal batch jobs can tolerate higher latency.

3) Peak behavior: our reconciliation runs cause large concurrency spikes roughly on the 1st and 15th. We need an ops runbook and fallback plan (e.g., degrade to cached responses or lower-cost model) during those windows.

Procurement contact: procurement@streamlinepay.com (CC'ing procurement here causes an auto-forward; procurement prefers DocuSign links + a short SOW).

I’ll have Jae share a rough traffic histogram so you can tune the token-econ sheet to real percentiles.

Alejandra
Head of Product, StreamlinePay

Subject: Pilot cost sketch + quick ROI bullets (attached model)

Alejandra / Jae / procurement team —

Attaching the token-econ workbook (streamlinepay_token_econ_model.xlsx) and a one-pager for pilot scope. I built the sheet with the traffic histogram you’ll share in mind; below are the highlights from the baseline vs three pilot configs.

Baseline (current provider, your avg session ~1.2k tokens):
- Estimated cost / 1M sessions: $14,800 (hosted endpoint, no batching, no cache)

Pilot A (small batching + local KV cache):
- Expected cost reduction: ~22% -> est. $11,544 / 1M sessions
- Latency impact: +10–20ms median; 95th stays under target for short flows

Pilot B (Aggressive batching + quantized model variant for background flows):
- Expected cost reduction: ~34% -> est. $9,768 / 1M sessions
- Latency: median similar; 95th for critical flows depends on route rules (we keep a warm pool for critical path)

Pilot C (Dedicated pool during reconciliation windows + batching):
- Expected cost: depends on reserved commit; for your peak profile we project 28–32% blended reduction vs baseline and strongly improved 95th stability

Other notes:
- Batching gains are driven by session grouping and reduced per-token kernel overhead; modeled sensitivity shows diminishing returns after ~2.5x batching due to tail latency needs.
- KV caching yields biggest wins when repeated prefixes > 15% of traffic. Please confirm anticipated prefix reuse from the histogram.

Recommended immediate asks for procurement: 
1) Confirm pilot budget band (lower/expected/upper): we modeled $90k / $120k / $150k per quarter scenarios.
2) Provide an SOW template or preferred DocuSign flow so we can prepare a targeted SOW and contract redlines.

If you want, Marissa and I can run a 30-min session next week to walk the workbook and show how changing the prefix reuse and batch factor changes the math in real-time.

Cheers,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
